messages:
alex: heads-up — i found 3 sa key json blobs inside a partner webhook gist we ingested for onboarding. they include project_id, client_email, and a private_key PEM. marking this P0, we should sweep and rotate.
maria: yikes. can you paste the gist url and which env this affects? also, do we know if those keys are already in use by any running jobs?
alex: gist: https://gist.github.com/partner/3f2a9... (redacted). it looks like staging creds but token in the file references project: redwood-staging-2 — suspicious. no obvious traffic spike yet but i ran a quick `gsutil ls` and saw a couple of accesses from a build IP yesterday.
jamal: @alex thanks. tagging SRE. @linda can you take immediate mitigation (block/deny) while we rotate?
linda: on it. i'm going to add a temporary org-level deny on that service account and create firewall rule to block the build agent IPs until we confirm impact. ETA 10m.
sre-bot: action: network block rule created -> fw-block-1698 (rule id fw-1698).
security-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0457 (secrets-leak). priority: high. link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-0457
maria: next steps from security: 1) revoke the exposed keys 2) create new keys and push to Vault (KMS-wrapped) 3) rewrap any existing wrapped blobs that referenced old key 4) scan infra for references and rotate consumers.
jamal: agree. i'll take rotation of the SA. plan: create a new key, update vault secret, push to partner if needed, then delete the exposed key. command i'll run (GCP):

```
# create new key
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create /tmp/new-sa-key.json --iam-account=my-sa@redwood-staging-2.iam.gserviceaccount.com
# update secrets: encrypt with KMS and put into Vault
gcloud kms encrypt --keyring=platform --key=secrets-enc --location=global --plaintext-file=/tmp/new-sa-key.json --ciphertext-file=/tmp/new-sa-key.json.enc
vault kv put secret/integrations/partner-a service_account=@/tmp/new-sa-key.json.enc
```

Note: we keep the raw JSON locally only in /tmp and ensure perms 600.

alex: for Vault write, we usually use transit rewrap if there are existing wrapped blobs referencing old key. @maria can you confirm rewrap plan?
maria: yes — if partners already used an encrypted blob we need to re-encrypt with the new key. steps:
1) list secrets referencing the SA: `vault kv list -format=json secret/ | jq '.[]'`
2) for each blob, `vault write transit/rewrap platform-key ciphertext=<old-cipher>`
3) verify new ciphertext is stored in secret path and consumers can decrypt.

linda: i've temporarily removed the exposed key from the account and set IAM to reject impersonation. i have not deleted the key yet (holding for forensic). firewall block is live.
jamal: good. forensic asks: capture any use of the exposed key before deletion. run logs:

```
# recent usage from key id
gcloud logging read "protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:my-sa@redwood-staging-2.iam.gserviceaccount.com" --limit 200 --project=redwood-staging-2
```

if we see service calls, capture IPs and caller service names.
security-bot: evidence captured: 4 entries found in last 72h. attached to incident INC-2026-0457.
oncall: i'm switching primary oncall to this incident, will coordinate with external partner contact. please paste partner POC and scope of what we will share.
alex: partner POC is clare@partnerco.com. we should only share that we rotated leaked credentials and ask them to pull the new wrapped blob from our Vault path — do not share raw key. we'll provide timestamped audit log lines.
maria: assign tasks:
- @jamal: create new SA key and rotate Vault entry (in progress)
- @linda: hold exposed key offline for forensics, continue network deny (done)
- @alex: run repo & artifact sweep (search for `private_key` patterns) and list hits
- @oncall: notify partner POC and coordinate secret handoff
- @security-bot: keep incident updated and run daily audit snapshot

jamal: i pushed new encrypted blob to `secret/integrations/partner-a` and updated terraform var in a canary service (staging). running smoke tests now. if green, i'll delete the compromised key (after forensics OK).
alex: smoke tests passing on canary.

maria: checklist before deleting exposed key:
- [ ] confirm no new uses in logs (run logging read after rotation)
- [ ] snapshot current Vault version and transit key metadata
- [ ] export forensic copy of exposed key to secure bucket (access: sec-only) and mark as evidence
- [ ] escalate to legal if partner data access observed

linda: forensic snapshot taken and uploaded to gs://sec-evidence/INC-2026-0457/exposed-key.json.enc (kms-wrapped). access restricted.
jamal: i've waited 30m post-rotation and re-run logging checks — no new calls from the compromised key. i'm going to delete it now:

```
gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete 0123456789abcdef --iam-account=my-sa@redwood-staging-2.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

alex: after delete, update the runbook and add an automated detection: create a log metric alert for `protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:my-sa@redwood-staging-2.iam.gserviceaccount.com` to catch replays.
maria: also rolling forward: policy changes — tighten SA key lifetime to 1d for non-prod, enforce use of workload identity where possible, and make Vault rotation a required CI step for onboarding partners.
security-bot: incident INC-2026-0457 status -> mitigation in progress; next update in 1h or on completion.
alex: thanks team. i'll run a final repo sweep and post findings in the incident doc. closing notes: avoid sharing raw keys in gists; use ephemeral exchange (signed URL to wrapped blob) instead.
jamal: noted. will follow-up with a small PR to the onboarding doc with the new ephemeral workflow and add an automated pre-commit scan for `PRIVATE_KEY` patterns.
linda: leaving firewall block for 24h, will lift after partner confirms they rotated. :lock:
maria: good job, everyone. postmortem template assigned, please add timelines and detection gaps. :+1:
